project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source reviewed here is the prepared open62541 checkout at `ac0d94217d06a229c9c671cfa0e37b497114848a` (`Stack: Correctly pass pointer to encoding for DiagnosticInfo`, 2019-05-06); its line map matches the saved ASan stack (`Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject:2994`, `String_clear:140`, `UA_decodeJson:3340`). ARVO metadata separately reports `89b73e8ba0b025983e1d81d7aa203e6a462da04d` / `36c440147e0adbd1c7254d98851c8a856e77cbfe`, but neither commit is an ancestor of the staged checkout. The staged `patch.diff` is commit `36c440147e0adbd1c7254d98851c8a856e77cbfe` (`fix(json): Fix a double-free in the JSON encoding`), and its added `dst->data = NULL;` lines match the reviewed stale-pointer cleanup bug exactly.

classification.classification_note: The staged patch message says "double-free", but the reproduced crash is a heap-use-after-free READ because the second cleanup first reads fields from the freed `UA_LocalizedText` object in `String_clear` before attempting any second free of its member buffers.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 44-byte ASCII string `{"Body"{"TypeId"{"Id":21}}"Body"[]"Type":22}`. In the reproduced vulnerable run, open62541 tokenizes that malformed JSON-like byte stream far enough for `Variant_decodeJson()` to recover top-level `Type = 22` and take the scalar ExtensionObject path. `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()` then decodes nested `TypeId.Id = 21`, resolves the body type to `UA_LocalizedText`, allocates a 32-byte `LocalizedText`, and later feeds the witness's `[]` body token into `LocalizedText_decodeJson()`, which returns `UA_STATUSCODE_BADDECODINGERROR` because the token is not an object. The vulnerable error path frees `dst->data` but leaves both `dst->data` and `dst->type` live in the same `UA_Variant`. `UA_decodeJson()` propagates the same non-GOOD status to its generic cleanup, calls `UA_deleteMembers(dst, type)`, and `Variant_clear()` reuses the freed `LocalizedText` pointer as a one-element array. `LocalizedText_clear -> String_clear` then reads fields from that freed 32-byte object, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/ua_types.c:140`. The staged patch fixes this by nulling `dst->data` immediately after both `UA_free(dst->data)` calls in `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()`.

source.description: First project parser step that consumes the attacker-controlled byte stream and materializes the jsmn token array later searched by the vulnerable JSON Variant decoder.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is exactly 44 bytes (sha256 `ea4515ff4e7feb762e7e7900d5db118ae2def7d79f88dcef137e5788cd052f3c`) and decodes as the ASCII string `{"Body"{"TypeId"{"Id":21}}"Body"[]"Type":22}`. The saved run proves this tokenization succeeds because execution reaches `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()` and later crashes in `String_clear()` during `UA_decodeJson()` cleanup.

root_cause.description: Error cleanup frees the just-allocated Variant body on decode failure but leaves the owning `UA_Variant` fields unchanged, so later generic cleanup reuses a dangling `LocalizedText` pointer.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `dst->data = NULL;` immediately after this free, and does the same in the parallel ExtensionObject branch, so `Variant_clear()` no longer sees a live pointer during `UA_decodeJson()` cleanup.

sink.description: ASan crash site. During the second cleanup, `String_clear` reads a `UA_String` member from the freed `UA_LocalizedText` still referenced by the output `UA_Variant`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 8` at `String_clear /src/open62541/src/ua_types.c:140:24`, 8 bytes inside the 32-byte region first allocated by `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject` and freed earlier in the same function.

parser_admitted.description: After tokenization succeeds and the top-level token is accepted as a JSON object, `UA_decodeJson()` dispatches the zeroed output value into `Variant_decodeJson()`.

unwrap_extensionobject.description: The attacker-controlled top-level `Type = 22` and scalar `Body` make the Variant decoder enter the unwrapped ExtensionObject body path instead of the scalar builtin or array paths.

if(ret != UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD)

second_cleanup.description: The BADDECODINGERROR from the nested LocalizedText body decode reaches `UA_decodeJson()` and triggers a second cleanup on the same `UA_Variant` after the inner error path already freed `dst->data`.

coarse_trace.summary: The malformed 44-byte witness is tokenized, passes the top-level object gate, and `Variant_decodeJson()` recovers `Type = 22` so the output `UA_Variant` is decoded through the scalar ExtensionObject path.

The unwrapped ExtensionObject path decodes `TypeId.Id = 21`, resolves the body type to `UA_LocalizedText`, allocates a 32-byte LocalizedText object, and then encounters a body-decode failure on the witness's `[]` token.
On that decode failure, the vulnerable code frees `dst->data` but leaves `dst->type` and `dst->data` live, then `UA_decodeJson()` takes its generic cleanup path on the same stale Variant.
Variant cleanup reuses the freed LocalizedText pointer as a one-element array, and `String_clear` reads the freed struct fields, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ 8.

fine_trace.note: Source. `jsmn_parse` consumes the exact staged witness `{"Body"{"TypeId"{"Id":21}}"Body"[]"Type":22}` and materializes the token array later traversed by `lookAheadForKey()` and `decodeFields()`. The saved run proves tokenization succeeds because execution reaches `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()` before the cleanup-time crash.

The top-level Variant decoder recovers attacker-controlled `Type = 22`, builds `UA_NODEID_NUMERIC(0, 22)`, and resolves `bodyType` to the built-in ExtensionObject type. That attacker-chosen type is what steers the output `UA_Variant` into ExtensionObject decoding instead of an ordinary scalar builtin type.

The same token stream yields a scalar `Body` token rather than a top-level array, so `isArray` stays false. Combined with step 2's `bodyType = ExtensionObject`, that makes the decoder hand the Variant body to `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()`.

Inside the unwrapped ExtensionObject path, the nested `TypeId` object decodes `Id = 21`, and `UA_findDataType(&typeId)` resolves that built-in type to `UA_LocalizedText`. No `Encoding` key is required here; with `encoding` left at 0, the function proceeds to allocate and decode the structure body directly.

Stores `dst->type = LocalizedText` in the output Variant and allocates a zeroed 32-byte `UA_LocalizedText` via `UA_new`/`UA_calloc`. ASan's allocation stack names this exact site as the origin of the later-freed heap region.

On the exact malformed token stream, the `UA_JSONKEY_BODY` decode inside this unwrapped ExtensionObject reaches the witness's `[]` token and invokes `LocalizedText_decodeJson()` on an array. `CHECK_OBJECT` therefore returns `UA_STATUSCODE_BADDECODINGERROR` immediately, while the Variant still owns the allocated pointer from step 5.

Root cause. The BADDECODINGERROR from step 6 takes this error branch, which frees the 32-byte LocalizedText allocation but does not clear `dst->data` or `dst->type`. The output Variant is left holding a stale owner pair `(type = LocalizedText, data = freed_ptr)`.

fine_trace.code:
if(ret != UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD)
    UA_deleteMembers(dst, type); /* Clean up */
fine_trace.note: That same non-GOOD status propagates back to `UA_decodeJson()`, which takes its generic error cleanup on the stale Variant instead of returning it untouched.

The cleanup sees `p->type = LocalizedText` and the non-null freed `p->data` from step 7. Because the Variant is scalar, it normalizes `arrayLength` to 1 and reuses the freed pointer as a one-element LocalizedText array base.

Sink. `UA_Array_delete` from step 9 walks the freed LocalizedText element, `LocalizedText_clear` calls `String_clear(&p->locale, NULL)`, and this statement reads `locale.data` and `locale.length` from the freed 32-byte object. ASan reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ 8 here.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `dst->data = NULL;` immediately after both `UA_free(dst->data)` calls in `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()`, which removes the stale pointer reused at steps 8-10.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executes `/out/fuzz_json_decode /tmp/poc` via `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_20061 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` with stack `String_clear -> LocalizedText_clear -> UA_clear -> Variant_clear -> UA_decodeJson`.

format.name: open62541 JSON Variant / ExtensionObject token stream
format.contract: Use the exact 44-byte ASCII witness `{"Body"{"TypeId"{"Id":21}}"Body"[]"Type":22}` (sha256 `ea4515ff4e7feb762e7e7900d5db118ae2def7d79f88dcef137e5788cd052f3c`). On the witnessed path, that malformed token stream is accepted far enough for `Variant_decodeJson()` to recover top-level `Type = 22`, for `Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject()` to resolve nested `TypeId.Id = 21`, and for the later `[]` body token to drive a `LocalizedText_decodeJson()` failure. The trigger semantics recorded here do not generalize beyond this exact staged byte sequence.
